html:
Ruler of the city of Texcoco in the Valley of Mexico from 1431 to 1472, remembered as a poet, lawmaker and builder.

As a teenager he watched the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco kill his father and take Texcoco. He spent years in exile. In 1428 he joined the Mexica of Tenochtitlan to defeat Azcapotzalco, and together with Tlacopan they formed the Triple Alliance that ruled central Mexico until 1521.

His works:

  • A long dike across Lake Texcoco that kept salty water away from Tenochtitlan.
  • An aqueduct bringing fresh water from Chapultepec to Tenochtitlan.
  • Gardens and baths cut into the hill of Texcotzingo.
  • A law code and councils for music, poetry and learning that made Texcoco the cultural capital of the region.

Poems in Nahuatl about the shortness of life are credited to him, though who wrote them is not certain. His face is on Mexico's 100 peso note.
sum: Ruler of the city of Texcoco in the Valley of Mexico from 1431 to 1472, remembered as a poet, lawmaker and builder.
